source.headline: Oil prices rise after Saudi Arabia shut down critical pipeline that bypasses Strait of Hormuz

summary: Saudi Arabia shut its critical East-West crude pipeline after drones launched from Iraq damaged the route. The pipeline is especially important because it bypasses the Strait of Hormuz; WTI was reported up 2.3% to $102.38 and Brent up 2.3% to $107.02 by 6:02 p.m. ET. The duration and severity of the outage were not yet disclosed at prediction time.

US2Y.source: U.S. Treasury par yield data via Treasury Rate Watch

US10Y.source: U.S. Treasury par yield data via Treasury Rate Watch

learning_adjustment.basis: Leakage-safe v2 confidence calibration shows weak short-horizon hit rates for directional confidence buckets 1-4 and 5-6, while low-confidence MIXED performs strongly. The physical pipeline shutdown is nevertheless a new, material supply shock, so current facts override a neutral classification; v2 evidence only capped directional confidence rather than changing direction.

predictions.mechanism: A shutdown of the Saudi bypass pipeline tightens physical oil supply, pushes energy prices and inflation expectations higher, and adds pressure to already-elevated Treasury yields, creating a direct risk-off headwind for broad U.S. equities.
predictions.invalidation: Rapid confirmation that the East-West pipeline is fully restored with WTI and Brent reversing the weekend spike would materially weaken the bearish signal.

predictions.mechanism: Growth equities are especially exposed to renewed inflation and discount-rate pressure when an oil supply shock arrives with the U.S. 10-year yield already near 5%.
predictions.invalidation: A fast pipeline restart and simultaneous decline in crude and Treasury yields would invalidate the immediate downside thesis.

predictions.mechanism: Germany and European cyclicals are vulnerable to higher imported energy costs; the outage affects a route designed specifically to bypass blocked Hormuz flows and therefore raises the effective supply-risk premium.
predictions.invalidation: Confirmed rapid restoration of Saudi export capacity or a major diplomatic de-escalation that drives crude back below the pre-shock level would weaken the call.

predictions.mechanism: Higher crude prices worsen the European inflation-growth tradeoff and reinforce pressure from tighter monetary policy, while the physical infrastructure outage raises near-term geopolitical risk.
predictions.invalidation: A quick pipeline reopening accompanied by a full reversal in Brent would remove the core physical-supply mechanism.

predictions.mechanism: French equities face the same energy and risk-premium shock as the broader euro area, though index sector composition makes the effect less direct than for the most rate-sensitive markets.
predictions.invalidation: Rapid restoration of the pipeline and normalization of oil prices would reduce the downside pressure.

predictions.mechanism: A confirmed attack-driven shutdown of critical Saudi export infrastructure increases geopolitical and tail-risk demand for gold, although very high U.S. yields limit confidence in the upside response.
predictions.invalidation: A fast repair, meaningful regional de-escalation and falling crude without a broader risk-off move would weaken safe-haven demand for gold.
